study_type.note: Claude also frames it as a single-company case study; NotebookLM calls it a single-company case study in its limitations.

research_method.claude: Multi-stage mixed methods: online survey (33 closed items, 6-point verbal scale), SonarQube static code analysis of repositories, qualitative focus group (reversed brainstorming); Spearman correlations; triangulation
research_method.nlm: Mixed methods: quantitative online survey (33 items, 6-point scale), static code analysis (SonarQube), qualitative focus group workshop (5-step reversed brainstorming)
research_method.value: Multi-stage mixed-methods study: online survey (33 closed items on a 6-point scale, based on Greiler et al.'s DX framework; 47 respondents), automated SonarQube static code analysis of 38 repositories, and an online focus group (7 developers) using 5-step reversed brainstorming; results triangulated
research_method.note: Spearman correlation analysis reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry; anonymous German medium-sized company (~100 developers, no dedicated DX team); 47 survey respondents, 38 public GitHub repositories, 7 focus-group participants
context.nlm: Industry; German medium-sized corporation (~100 developers); 47 survey respondents, 38 repositories, 7 focus-group developers
context.value: industry; anonymous German medium-sized corporation (~100 developers, no dedicated DX team); 47 survey respondents, 38 public GitHub repositories, 7 focus-group participants

space_applied.note: SPACE only referenced in related work.

ai_discussed.note: Internal AI documentation assistant used by developers; broadening its access is one of the five measures derived. Not used as a research method.

remote_covid.note: Only passing mentions (working from home inside the work-life-balance item; online focus group; 'distributed team structures' in intro).

data_window.note: Not stated by either (static analysis described as a cross-sectional snapshot, no dates).

cat_productivity.note: No output/throughput metric; perceived efficiency appears only as a correlated survey item.

cat_quality.note: SonarQube complexity, duplication, maintainability, reliability (bugs, defects per KLOC), security.

cat_collaboration.note: 'Collaboration and Culture' survey group (psychological safety, documentation/knowledge sharing) and code review presence.

cat_satisfaction.note: Work-life balance and meaningfulness of tasks survey items.

cat_activity.note: Borderline: both list LOC/KLOC (Size) as Activity, but it is repository size used only to normalize SonarQube results, not developer activity.

cat_delivery.note: Only perceived local setup/CI-CD effort (greenfield vs legacy) survey items; no lead time, deployment or release metric.

cat_devex.note: Survey built on Greiler, Storey & Noda's DX framework (applied); Noda/Forsgren/Storey/Greiler three dimensions (feedback loops, cognitive load, flow state) used to interpret findings. Strictly, the applied framework is Greiler et al.'s, not the 2023 DevEx paper.

cat_agile.note: Claude: 'Product Management' survey group and realistic time planning item (process). NotebookLM: no process or planning metric.

cat_survey.note: Online survey with 6-option Likert-type items, plus focus group.

evidence.quote: The initial stage comprised a thorough, predominantly quantitative survey supplemented by project analyses. The second stage of the research involved the execution of a qualitative focus group workshop.

A total of 47 employees completed the survey in full, with no indication of systematic non-response bias. The focus group, comprising seven participants, was utilized to further explore the prevailing circumstances.
a medium-sized corporation with approximately one hundred developers, where establishing dedicated DX teams is not a viable option
The static code analysis encompassed 38 repositories, thereby providing an objective perspective on the structural integrity of code across the organization.
Furthermore, the focus group confirmed the relevance of an AIbased assistant, which is already in use within the organization to support developers accessing and summarizing documentation.
Complexity (e.g., cyclomatic and cognitive complexity, nesting), where higher values indicate reduced understandability and elevated defect risk.
Can you ask questions without fear of being judged or facing negative consequences, regardless of your level of experience or position?
evidence.loc: PDF p. 3 (3.1, Collaboration and Culture items)

evidence.quote: indicating that the absence of review structures has a detrimental effect on feedback culture, knowledge transfer, and perceived quality assurance.

The aspects that were most highly rated by respondents include the professional and technical challenges associated with the work (1.53), the work-life balance (1.6), and the perceived meaningfulness of tasks (1.81).
The questions are based mostly on the DX factors from Greilers DX-Framework [11]
These factors directly shape the core DX dimensions of feedback loops, cognitive load, and flow state.
Single-choice questions with a Likert scale and an even number of answer options (i.e. no middle option) were preferred where meaningful.
